summary: Created tests/tools/schema-integrity.test.ts — a 24-test regression guard that captures all 22 tool schemas by calling register() with a mock MCP server, converts each to JSON Schema via zodToJsonSchema, and asserts non-empty properties. The test for resolveProjectPath() throwing when both paths provided was already added during WP-001. All 1038 tests pass across 34 test files. TypeScript compiles clean.

comments.note: Used mock McpServer approach to capture inputSchema from all register() calls rather than exporting schemas directly. This mirrors the exact runtime registration path and requires no source changes to expose schemas. The 24-test suite covers all 22 tools plus two structural checks (count and name enumeration). zod-to-json-schema is used as a transitive dependency (via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk) — not added as an explicit devDependency. Consider formalising this via a devDependency entry in package.json if desired for clarity.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified and met. Build check: TypeScript compiles clean (npx tsc --noEmit, no output). AC verification: (1) resolveProjectPath() throws MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG when both paths provided — confirmed at line 200-202 of path-validator.test.ts; (2) resolveProjectPath() succeeds with single project_path (lines 144-147) and single cwd_path (lines 161-178); (3) schema-integrity.test.ts exists with 24 tests (22 tool schemas + 2 structural checks); (4) all 22 schemas produce non-empty JSON Schema properties — confirmed by all 24 schema tests passing; (5) all existing mutuallyExclusivePaths tests pass unchanged (30 tests in path-validator.test.ts). Regression: npm test passes — 1038 tests across 34 test files, all green. Edge cases: (a) strict size check (toBe(22)) ensures a newly added tool without updating EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES will break the count test — guard is effective; (b) zod-to-json-schema is a transitive dependency (via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk) and is present in node_modules — tests run correctly, though it is not formalised as a devDependency in package.json (low-risk fragility noted)."

comments.note: zod-to-json-schema is consumed as a transitive dependency (via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk) rather than a declared devDependency. This works today and the tests pass, but if the SDK is updated and drops this dep the schema-integrity test suite would break at import. Consider adding zod-to-json-schema as an explicit devDependency in mcp-server/package.json for long-term stability. Developer's implementation comment already flags this.

summary: Code review PASS. The schema-integrity.test.ts file is well-crafted: exemplary file header with root-cause explanation and constraint cross-references; correct use of beforeAll for single-shot registration; tight two-layer structural guard (count + per-name coverage); and a mock McpServer that exercises the exact production registration path without source changes. No blocking issues found. One non-blocking suggestion carried forward from Developer and QA: add zod-to-json-schema as an explicit devDependency in mcp-server/package.json to eliminate transitive-dependency fragility.

comments.note: zod-to-json-schema is imported directly in schema-integrity.test.ts but is not declared as a devDependency in mcp-server/package.json. It currently resolves as a transitive dep of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. If the SDK is updated and drops this dep, the test suite breaks at import without a clear error message. Recommend: add `"zod-to-json-schema": "*"` (or pin to the current resolved version) under devDependencies. This is non-blocking — the tests pass today and the risk is low — but it is the right long-term hygiene step.

Gold Nugget: The mock McpServer intercept pattern used here (capturing inputSchema at register() time via a Map) is reusable for any future test that needs to inspect tool metadata (e.g., description content, parameter constraints) without spinning up a real server. Consider documenting this pattern in mcp-server/docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md or a dedicated 'testing patterns' note.
